newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's auto sales up, aided by strong exports.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's auto sales up, aided by strong exports.

text.p: South Korea's major carmakers on Tuesday posted strong sales figures for June aided by soaring exports, but domestic sales remained lacklustre due to the slowing economy.
Hyundai Motor Co Ltd, South Korea's largest carmaker, said its vehicle sales in June rose 8.3 percent to 118,764 units from 109,696 a year earlier.
A Hyundai spokesman said exports soared 42 percent to 61,993 units from 43,609 units, thanks to the company's drive to explore relatively new markets, such as Turkey, Greece, Spain and Italy.
Kia Motors Corp also reported a surge in its June sales, which rose 73 percent to 67,746 units from 39,125 a year earlier.
Kia Motors is the flagship and strongest unit of the embattled Kia Group, which has been struggling in recent months against rumours financial troubles and skittish lenders.
Kia said its exports jumped 343 percent to 40,093 units from 9,048 a year ago, when a wildcat strike hampered shipments.
"Labour disputes damaged exports last June. But this year's exports are well above the average due to our efforts to explore new markets," said a Kia spokesman.
Analysts said auto manufacturers were concentrating on overseas sales because of a protracted slump in the domestic market.
"Carmakers' export drive became more conspicuous in June, as the domestic market shows no signs of recovery yet," said Yang Dong-ki, analyst at Dongbang Peregrine Securities.
Domestic sales of Hyundai and Kia dropped as they lost ground to Daewoo Motor Co of the Daewoo Group. Daewoo's new model cars have proven popular in the local market.
Hyundai's domestic sales fell 14 percent to 56,771 units from 66,087 units.
"Our domestic sales were affected by the introduction of Daewoo Motor's new models," said a Hyundai spokesman.

Kia's domestic sales fell eight percent to 27,653 units from 30,077 units for similar reasons, said the Kia spokesman. But he added his company's domestic sales would improve in the second half with the advent of its own new models, including a new version of its Sephia compact car.
Daewoo Motor said its vehicles sales in June fell 2.5 percent to 85,542 units from 87,754 units a year earlier.
A Daewoo statement said exports dropped 10.5 percent to 54,063 units in the month from 60,379 units a year before due to a lack of cargo ships.
The fall in exports was inevitable because the company had yet to replace all of its old export models, a Daewoo spokesman said.
However, Daewoo's domestic sales rose 15 percent to 31,479 units from 27,375 units a year ago.
"The debut of new model cars, including the Leganza and Nubira, helped our domestic sales," the Daewoo spokesman said.
Sales of Leganza mid-sized sedans, which began selling in April, totalled 10,024 units in June and smaller Nubira cars, which rolled out from February, amounted to 8,025 units.
"Our share in the domestic passenger car market rose to 35.1 percent in June from 26.8 percent thanks to the new models," said a Daewoo official.
Hyundai's vehicle sales in the first half of this year totalled 593,989 units, down from 636,610 units a year ago.
Daewoo sold 461,977 units in the January-June period, compared with 382,664 units a year ago, while Kia's sales rose to 361,872 units from 355,785.
